part2.intro: Three teenagers write about an interesting building they have visited.
part2.question: For each question, choose the correct answer.

texts.label: A
texts.title: Isabel
texts.text: Last summer I visited a castle in Scotland with my family. It's on a high hill, so we had to walk up a long road to get to the entrance. Inside, there were old rooms with swords and paintings of kings and queens. My favourite part was the dark prison under the castle – it was a bit scary! The view from the top was brilliant. You can see the whole city from there.

texts.label: B
texts.title: Duc
texts.text: Last month I visited a new art museum in Hanoi with my class. The building is very modern, with glass walls, so it's full of light. We saw paintings by young Vietnamese artists, and then we painted our own pictures in a special room. Mine was terrible, but the teacher put it on the wall anyway! I'd like to go back with my parents because they both love art.

texts.label: C
texts.title: Hannah
texts.text: For my birthday, my brother took me on a tour of a famous football stadium. We saw the players' changing rooms and walked onto the pitch. It felt amazing! The guide told us lots of funny stories about the players. At the end, we had lunch in the stadium cafe. It was quite expensive, but my brother paid, so I didn't mind! It was the best present ever.

items.q: Who visited the building as a birthday present?

Who made something during their visit?

Who could see a long way from the building?

part3.title: The boy who builds cathedrals
part3.text:
When fifteen-year-old Arjun Mehta was eight, his grandfather gave him a book about famous buildings. 'I loved the pictures,' says Arjun. 'Every night I looked at the castles and churches and wanted to make them myself.'

His first model was a small house made of paper. 'It wasn't very good,' he laughs. 'It fell down the next day!' But Arjun didn't stop. Now he makes models from wood and card, and they are excellent.

His biggest model is of the old cathedral in his town. It took him eleven months to finish, and it is almost two metres tall. 'The most difficult part was the windows,' he says. 'There are more than two hundred of them, and I had to cut every one by hand.' He worked on the model every weekend and sometimes after school – but only when his homework was finished. That was his mum's rule.

Last spring, the town museum asked if they could show the model. Thousands of people came to see it, and the local newspaper wrote a story about Arjun. 'I was really surprised,' he says. 'I didn't think people would be so interested.'

Arjun now wants to study at university to become an architect – a person who plans and designs buildings. 'I want to make real buildings, not just models,' he says. 'Maybe one day there'll be a model of one of my buildings in a museum!'

items.q: Why did Arjun become interested in buildings?
options: He visited a lot of castles when he was young.
A family member gave him a book.

items.q: What happened to Arjun's first model?
options: He gave it to his grandfather.

items.q: What was the hardest thing about the cathedral model?
options: finding enough time to work on it

items.q: What rule did Arjun's mother have?
options: He could only work on models at weekends.
He had to do his homework first.
He couldn't keep models in his bedroom.

items.q: How did Arjun feel when so many people came to see his model?
options: He didn't expect so much interest.
He was worried that someone would break it.
He wanted to sell it to the museum.

part4.title: Libraries – then and now
part4.text:
Libraries have been important for thousands of years. One of the most {19} libraries in history was in Alexandria, in Egypt. It was built more than 2,000 years ago, and it had thousands of books. They were not like our books – they were {20} on long rolls of paper.

Hundreds of years ago, books were very expensive, so only rich people could {21} them. Most people never had a book at home. Then, in the 1800s, many towns in Britain built free public libraries, so everyone could read.

Today, libraries are very different. Most of them have computers, and you can {22} films and music as well as books. Many libraries also have special events for children and teenagers, {23} as book clubs and writing classes.

Some people think that libraries are not important any more because we can find everything on the internet. But libraries are still a great {24} to study, meet friends and find new books to read.

items.q: Where are the boy and his mum going to meet?

script.t: Sam, I'll be at the bank until three. Shall we meet outside it?
It's going to rain, Mum. Can we meet inside somewhere? What about the bookshop?
It's closed this week. They're painting it. Let's meet in the cafe next to it.

items.q: Which floor does the girl live on?

script.t: Which floor is your new flat on, Nina?
The ninth. Our old flat was on the second floor, so it's very different.
Wow. Do you take the lift?
Usually. But my friend Lucy lives on the fifth floor of the same building, so sometimes I walk down to her flat.

items.q: What is the new building in the town centre going to be?

script.t: Have you seen that big new building in the town centre? Is it a hotel?
That's what everyone thought. But my dad says it's going to be a cinema, with eight screens.
Great! I hoped it would be a swimming pool, but a cinema's good too.
It opens in June.

items.q: Where did the boy go yesterday?

script.t: Did you go to the castle with your grandparents yesterday, Tim?
We wanted to, but it was closed. So we went to the museum instead.
Was it good?
Yes, really interesting. Then Grandma wanted to see the old church, but we were too tired, so we went home.

items.q: What is the girl going to do at the sports centre?

script.t: Are you going swimming at the sports centre on Saturday, Jess?
Not this week – I've got a cold. But I'm going to play badminton there with my dad.
I thought you wanted to try the climbing wall.
I do, but you have to be fourteen. Next year!

part2.intro: You will hear a guide talking to a group of visitors at a castle.
part2.title: Bradley Castle Tour

items.label: People started building the castle in:
Number of steps in the tower:
The gift shop is next to the:

script.t: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to Bradley Castle. My name's Paul and I'm your guide today. This castle is very old. People started building it in eleven fifty, and it took about forty years to finish. Lots of visitors think it's much newer, because the outside is so clean! We'll begin our tour in the great hall, and then we'll visit the kitchens. After that, you can climb the tower. There are ninety-five steps – I know because I count them every day! Please be careful, because they're quite small. From the top you can see the cathedral and the university buildings in the city. You're welcome to take photos everywhere except the library. The old books there don't like the light from cameras. If you want to buy a present, the gift shop isn't near the entrance where you came in. It's next to the exit, at the end of the tour. And if you're hungry, the castle cafe is open until half past four today. It usually closes at five, but there's a special event this evening. OK, follow me, please!

part3.intro: You will hear Oliver talking to his friend Grace about his work experience in an office.

items.q: Where was Oliver's office?
What did Oliver do during his work experience?
options: He helped to make a website.
He helped to design a hotel.

items.q: What was the problem with the cafe in the building?
Where did Oliver eat his lunch?
What didn't Oliver like about working in an office?

script.t: Hi Oliver. How was your week of work experience?
Really good, thanks, Grace. I was at a big company in the city centre. Their offices are in a really tall building – it's got thirty floors!
Wow. Were you at the top?
No, the company is on the twenty-second floor. I went up in the lift every morning. On the first day it was so fast I felt a bit sick!
Ha! So what did you do? Did you just make coffee?
My brother said I'd only make tea and coffee all week, but I didn't make any! I helped to make a website for a new hotel. It was really interesting.
That's cool. Were the people nice?
Very friendly. My manager, Lisa, was great. She explained everything clearly. The only problem was lunch. There's a cafe on the ground floor, and it's never too busy, but it was really expensive.
So what did you do?
After the first day, I took sandwiches from home and ate them in the park next to the cathedral. It was lovely and quiet there.
Would you like to work in an office one day?
I'm not sure. I loved the work, but I didn't like sitting down all day. I like moving around.
So what are you going to do?
Well, I'd like to study computers at university or college. Then maybe I can work from home!

items.intro: You will hear a boy talking about the old cinema in his town.
items.q: How does he feel about the cinema closing?
options: He's angry about the new cinema.

script.t: The old cinema in our town is closing next month. Lots of people say it's sad, but I don't really agree. It was always cold inside, and the seats were terrible. A new cinema is opening in the shopping centre, with bigger screens and better seats. I'm actually quite happy about it.

items.intro: You will hear a girl telling her father about a building.
items.q: What was the building in the past?

script.t: Dad, did you know our new library was a hospital before?
Really? I thought it was an old school.
No, the school was on the other side of the road. My teacher told us the building was a hospital for a hundred years.
How interesting! I didn't know that.

script.t: Have you been to the new sports centre yet?
Yes, on Saturday. It's much better than the old one – the gym is brilliant.
Isn't the swimming pool quite small?
No, it's the same size as before. And it's only five minutes from my house, so I'm going to go every week.

script.t: OK, everyone, you can now look around the museum on your own. Please don't go into the shop – we'll visit it together at the end. At two o'clock, meet me at the main entrance, next to the big dinosaur. Don't go to the exit, because it's on the other side of the building and our bus is waiting at the front.

part5.intro: You will hear Max telling his mum about his family's day in the city. Where did each person go?

script.t: How was your day in the city, Max? I'm sorry I had to work.
It was great, Mum. We all went to different places. Dad went to the university. He wanted to see the building where he studied.
Oh, I thought he wanted to go to the cathedral.
He did, but there was a wedding, so he couldn't go in. So he went to the university and met an old friend there.
And Grandpa? He loves old cars.
Yes! He went to the car factory just outside the city. They have tours on Saturdays. He said it was brilliant.
What about Uncle Peter?
He went to the theatre in the afternoon to see a play. He wanted me to go with him, but I said no. Plays are boring!
And Ruby? Did she go shopping?
She wanted to go to the big department store, but everything there is too expensive. So she went to her friend's college to see an art show. Her friend's paintings were in it.
That's nice. And Josh? Did he go with you?
Yes. We went to the museum together – there's a new dinosaur room. Josh wanted to go to the teen disco in the evening too, but we were too tired!
